summary: A TypeScript library (cache-kit, private package, zero runtime dependencies, Node 20.3+) for an in-process cache in front of any expensive call (a DB query, a call to another service, a config lookup), usable from Express, NestJS, workers or scripts. Stage 1: LruCache -- LRU order is a JavaScript Map's insertion order (a hit deletes and re-inserts the key), maxEntries required, an optional maxWeight with weigh() that must return an integer >= 0 (anything else is a RangeError and the cache is unchanged; fractions are refused because a running float total drifts), a single value heavier than maxWeight is not stored and the key's older value is removed; TTL with lazy expiry (expired AT set time + ttlMs, counted from set, not from reads), a monotonic performance.now clock (injectable), and an optional unref'd sweep timer stopped by close(); single-flight getOrLoad (100 concurrent misses -> 1 loader call, 99 coalesced; a loader error is shared by every waiter and never cached); per-caller abort (a caller that aborts only stops its own wait; the load's own signal is aborted only when EVERY waiter has left, and an abandoned load writes nothing); load versions against stale writes (the flight object is the key's version: delete, set and clear detach it, so a slow load that started before a delete cannot write the old value back); stats counters (hits and misses are counters, not events) and events (a throwing handler is ignored); and a randomized test that runs 8 seeds x 3000 steps against a naive array model and requires identical return values, key order, total weight and stats after every step. The benchmark (bench/overhead.mjs: 10 000 entries, 1 000 000 ops per round, median of 7 rounds; Windows 11, AMD Ryzen 5 4500, Node 20.20.1, a busy machine, Map.get floor 36.9 / 78.9 ns) found that eviction was not O(1): picking the victim with a new map.keys().next() per eviction cost 10401.9 ns per evicting set; with one long-lived keys() iterator it is 548.8 / 664.6 ns (two runs). The likely cause (V8 leaves holes for deleted entries and a new iterator starts at slot 0) is from how V8 is known to work, not from reading V8's source; a test counting Map.prototype.keys calls during 1000 evictions guards the fix without any timing assertion. Stage 2: stale-while-revalidate (fresh until the TTL, then served stale by getOrLoad for staleMs while ONE background refresh runs -- 50 concurrent stale reads -> 1 refresh; a failed refresh keeps the stale value until the grace ends and the next stale read retries with no backoff; the refresh is an ordinary flight, so set / delete / clear win over it; get / peek / has never return a stale entry); negative caching (a LOADED value that isNegative -- default null or undefined -- is stored for min(its TTL, negativeTtlMs) with no grace; 1000 sequential + 100 concurrent lookups of a missing id -> 1 loader call; errors are still not cached); a load context (ttlMs, refresh, isCurrent()); and TwoLevelCache: L1 = an LruCache, L2 = Redis shared by replicas through a bring-your-own client (structural interfaces, ioredis adapters, ioredis 5.4.1 only a dev dependency), required key prefix, jsonCodec envelope by default, the Redis read runs inside the L1 load (50 concurrent misses on one replica -> 1 Redis read + 1 loader call), a Redis hit's L1 copy gets min(Redis PTTL, the call's TTL), writes after a load go to Redis in the background, and set / delete PUBLISH an invalidation that drops the key from every other replica's L1 (own messages ignored by a random instance id). The real-Redis test found a cross-replica race: replica B's background write of an OLD row reached Redis after replica A's set, and Redis then served the old value to every replica for a whole TTL; fixed by writing after a load with SET NX and making delete write a tombstone (default 10 s) instead of DEL; in four recorded runs of the 20-round race test the NX refusal was hit in 6, 14, 17 and 11 rounds and Redis held A's value every time. On every re-subscribe the replica clears its whole L1; the ioredis adapter does this only after Redis confirmed the new SUBSCRIBE, because ioredis emits ready before it sends its own re-SUBSCRIBE. Every Redis call is bounded by l2TimeoutMs (default 250 ms); an outage degrades to L1 + loader, set / delete resolve false and never throw for Redis. Stage 3: Express cachedJson (cache-kit/express, Node http types, tested with Express 4.21.2), NestJS @CachedRoute (an interceptor INSTANCE, no DI; tested with NestJS 10.4.15 on platform-express) and a framework-free legacy @Cached method decorator; they cache the handler's DATA, not HTTP bytes; the key function is required and must contain everything the producer reads (per-user data needs the user in the key); @Cached calls its key function with the instance as this (so per-instance state like a tenant can be in the key; the first version could not see this at all -- found by a bank reviewer, fixed, mutation D5) and always returns a promise (a sync throw is a rejection, D6); X-Cache: hit / stale / miss / bypass (stale = a stale value served at once while THIS request's background refresh ran the producer; the first version labelled that 'miss' because the refresh calls the loader synchronously -- found by a bank reviewer, fixed, mutation C7; with TwoLevelCache a stale serve whose refresh is answered by Redis shows hit); null / undefined -> 404 and cached like any value; producer errors not cached; the request's disconnect signal goes into getOrLoad; in Express nothing is written to and next(err) is not called for a client that has gone (in NestJS this is not special-cased: the aborted wait goes to the exception layer, a no-op write, and handlers get no abort signal); 20 concurrent requests -> 1 producer call; two Express instances on one real Redis: B answers from Redis without running its producer. 178 tests pass (Windows, Node 20; stage 1: 67, stage 2 added 84, stage 3 added 27; the 8 real-Redis tests ran against Redis 7.4.12). Mutation checks: stage 1, 42 breaks, 39 caught, 3 equivalent (L6, L7, W8, each explained); stage 2, 99 breaks (the 42 stage-1 ones re-based plus 57 new), every one that changes behaviour caught (96), the same 3 equivalent remain, and the 4 first-run survivors (X15, X16, X24, X25) were test gaps that were closed; stage 3, 20 breaks, all caught (3 first-run survivors, C4, E1, E2, the 'client already gone' paths, were closed by test/adapters-unit.test.ts with a fake response; C7, D5 and D6 guard the three interview-bank review fixes); 119 distinct breaks over all stages (99 + 20). Mutation W5 (weight not subtracted on remove) first HUNG the test run in an infinite eviction loop, which led to a size > 1 guard and integer-only weights. Not implemented: error caching (left out on purpose), backoff between failed refreshes, refresh-ahead, Redis Cluster / Sentinel specifics, RESP3 client-side caching (CLIENT TRACKING), Redis Streams instead of pub/sub, a clear across replicas, L2 for non-string keys, HTTP caching semantics (Cache-Control, ETag, Vary, conditional requests) and caching of non-JSON or streamed responses, NestJS on Fastify, an Express 5 test, sliding expiry, LFU / W-TinyLFU admission, a size estimate that walks objects, any measurement of stage 2 overhead or Redis round trips (and of concurrency, memory per entry, Linux), npm publishing.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek in-process cache library banayi hai, TypeScript mein, bina runtime dependency -- kisi bhi mehngi call ke aage, jaise DB query ya doosri service. LRU jo entries aur bytes dono se bounded hai, TTL, aur single-flight loading taaki 100 concurrent misses par query ek hi baar chale. Upar se stale-while-revalidate, negative caching, replicas ke beech shared Redis L2 pub/sub invalidation ke saath, aur Express / NestJS helpers. 178 tests, aur har behaviour badalne wala mutation caught.
pitch.explain_2min:
Zyada tar backend latency repeated kaam hai: wahi query, wahi config lookup, hazaaron baar. Naive cache -- ek Map plus setTimeout -- teen jagah toot-ta hai: memory bina limit badhti hai, expired value serve ho jaati hai, aur cold key par 100 requests ek saath 100 identical queries DB ko bhejti hain, yaani cache stampede.

Stage 1 mein LruCache. LRU order JavaScript Map ka insertion order hai: hit par delete + set, key end par chali jaati hai. maxEntries required, maxWeight optional (bytes; weigh integer hi lautaaye). TTL har read par lazily check hota hai, monotonic clock se, aur ek optional unref'd sweep. getOrLoad single flight hai: 100 concurrent misses -> 1 loader call. Ek caller abort kare toh sirf uska wait rukta hai; load tab abort hota hai jab saare waiters chale jaayein. delete ya set running load ko detach karte hain, toh slow load purani row wapas nahi likh sakta. Ek randomized test 8 seeds x 3000 steps mein cache ko ek naive array model se compare karta hai.

Stage 2: stale-while-revalidate -- TTL ke baad grace mein purani value turant, aur sirf ek background refresh. Negative caching -- 'not found' chhote TTL ke liye; errors kabhi cache nahi hote. TwoLevelCache: L1 process ke andar, L2 Redis jo saare replicas share karte hain, aur set / delete par pub/sub se baaki replicas ka L1 saaf. Real Redis test ne ek cross-replica race pakdi, jo SET NX aur tombstones se fix hui. Redis down ho toh read fail nahi hota: L1 + loader.

Stage 3: Express cachedJson, NestJS @CachedRoute aur @Cached -- handler ka data cache hota hai, HTTP bytes nahi, aur key required hai.

Benchmark ne surprise diya: eviction O(1) nahi thi, 10401.9 ns per evicting set; ek long-lived iterator ke baad 548.8 / 664.6 ns. Design aur review maine kiya -- stages 1 aur 2 delegated agents ne implement kiye, maine review karke merge kiye. 178 tests, mutation checks mein har real break caught.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek GET /products/42 ki journey, Express se Redis tak aur doosre replica tak.

Setup. Module level par ek baar: productCache = new TwoLevelCache({ l1: new LruCache({ maxEntries: 10000, ttlMs: 30000 }), redis: ioredisL2Client(redis), subscriber: ioredisSubscriber(redis.duplicate()), prefix: 'myapp:products:' }). Do connections kyunki SUBSCRIBE chalane wala connection subscriber mode mein chala jaata hai aur GET / SET nahi chala sakta. Route: app.get('/products/:id', cachedJson(productCache, { key: (req) => 'product:' + req.params.id, ttlMs: 60000 }, (req, signal) => db.products.find(req.params.id, { signal }))).

cachedJson. Handler pehle requestSignal(res) banata hai: response ke close par, agar response finish nahi hua, toh AbortController abort. Phir loadForRequest: key function se 'product:42'; undefined hota toh producer seedha chalta aur X-Cache: bypass. Ek ran flag rakha jaata hai -- producer is request ne chalaya aur usne wait kiya toh miss, is request ke background refresh ne chalaya (stale value turant mili) toh stale, warna hit. Pehli version mein 'stale' tha hi nahi: refresh loader ko synchronously bulata hai, toh ran flag set ho jaata aur stale serve 'miss' dikhta -- bank review mein pakda, fix aur mutation C7.

TwoLevelCache.getOrLoad seedha l1.getOrLoad ko bulata hai, loader ki jagah apna loadThrough deke. Yahi trick hai: Redis read L1 ke load ke ANDAR chalta hai, toh single flight Redis ko bhi cover karta hai -- 50 concurrent misses ek replica par = 1 Redis read.

LruCache.getOrLoad. Pehle signal.throwIfAborted. Phir live(key): entry deadAt ke paar ho toh 'expired' ke saath evict. Fresh ho toh hit: delete + set se most recent, return. Stale ho toh purani value turant, aur flight na chal rahi ho toh ek background refresh. Miss par flights map dekha jaata hai: load chal raha hai toh join (coalesced), warna startLoad: ek Flight object (AbortController, waiters count), loads++, 'load' event, aur LoadContext { ttlMs, refresh, isCurrent }. isCurrent() bas itna hai: flights.get(key) === flight.

loadThrough. readL2: MULTI GET + PTTL, l2TimeoutMs (250) ke andar. Value null, TOMBSTONE, ya PTTL 0 -> miss. Decode fail -> 'corrupt'. Hit ho toh context.ttlMs = min(PTTL, call TTL) -- L1 copy Redis copy se zyada na jiye -- aur loader chalta hi nahi. Miss par signal.throwIfAborted (sab chale gaye toh DB ko bekaar call nahi), phir producer: db query, ran = true.

Write-behind. Agar context.isCurrent() abhi bhi true hai, toh writeBehind: encode, aur SET prefix+key value PX ttl NX -- await nahi hota, callers ko Redis ka wait nahi; pending set mein track, flush() ke liye. Redis null lautaaye toh l2WritesSkipped. Phir LruCache mein: flight abhi bhi attached hai toh TTL check, negative check, weigh, store; maxEntries ya maxWeight ke upar ho toh long-lived iterator se least recently used evict.

Response. res.writableEnded ya destroyed ho toh kuch nahi likhte. Value null ho toh 404 not_found (aur woh cache bhi hota hai), warna 200, X-Cache: miss, JSON. Error ho toh next(err), lekin client ja chuka ho toh woh bhi nahi.

Ab doosra replica. Admin replica A par product update karta hai, aur A.set('product:42', newValue): A ka L1, Redis mein plain SET PX (NX nahi -- yeh naya value hai, late load nahi), phir PUBLISH [A ka instance id, key]. Replica B ka subscriber message parse karta hai; apna id ho toh ignore, warna l1.delete(key). Woh delete running flight ko bhi detach karta hai, toh agar B abhi wahi key load kar raha tha, uska isCurrent() false -- B na L1 likhta hai na Redis. Aur agar B ka NX write message se pehle hi nikal chuka tha aur A ke SET ke baad pahunchta hai, toh NX refuse ho jaata hai. delete mein DEL ki jagah tombstone, taaki wahi late write delete ke baad bhi refuse ho.

Sabse mushkil decisions. Pehla, yeh race: pehli version load ke baad plain SET karti thi, aur real Redis test fail hua -- B ka write apne connection par A ke set ke baad pahuncha aur poore TTL ke liye purani value sab replicas ko gayi. Lua compare-and-set with versions aur 'delayed double delete' ki jagah SET NX + tombstone chuna: kam moving parts, aur double delete mein sleep ke baad bhi window rehti hai. Doosra, abort: pehle caller ke abort par load cancel karna ek impatient client se sabko fail karwa deta; kabhi cancel na karna aisa kaam jo koi nahi chahta -- isliye load tab cancel jab saare waiters jaayein. Teesra, get stale value nahi lautata: get ke paas loader nahi, refresh nahi kar sakta, toh warna ttlMs ka matlab hi khatam. Chautha, Redis kabhi read fail nahi karta -- DB write ho chuka hai, cache problem ke liye 500 galat hota. Paanchwa, helpers mein data cache, bytes nahi, aur key required -- URL-only default ek user ka data doosre ko de deta.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/events.ts: CacheEvent union (evict with reason size / weight / expired, reject, load, load-error, refresh, refresh-error, load-abort), EvictionReason, aur emit() jo throwing handler ko ignore karta hai -- telemetry kabhi caller ka result nahi badalti. src/cache.ts: LruCache -- options validation (maxEntries integer >= 1, maxWeight needs weigh, ttlMs > 0, staleMs >= 0, isNegative needs negativeTtlMs), Entry { value, weight, expiresAt, deadAt, negative }, Flight { controller, promise, waiters, settled } jo key ka load version hai; get / peek / has sirf fresh entry dete hain (fresh() over live()); set flights.delete karke store karta hai; delete aur clear bhi flights detach karte hain; purgeExpired O(n) aur sweep timer unref'd; getOrLoad -> startLoad (LoadContext, refresh ke liye ek permanent waiter) -> wait (per-caller abort listener, settle par remove) -> leave (aakhri waiter gaya toh controller.abort, load-abort); store() mein reject, size loop, aur weight loop jismein size > 1 guard (W5 ke baad); evictOldest ek long-lived keys() iterator use karta hai (benchmark finding); weighOf integer check. src/two-level.ts: L2Client (getWithTtl, set with ttl + NX, publish) aur L2Subscriber (subscribe with onResubscribed) interfaces; ioredisL2Client (MULTI GET + PTTL, SET PX / NX mapping) aur ioredisSubscriber (pehla ready ignore, reconnect par khud SUBSCRIBE bhej ke confirm hone par onResubscribed); jsonCodec ({v: ...} envelope); TOMBSTONE (NUL se shuru string); TwoLevelCache -- getOrLoad = l1.getOrLoad + loadThrough, readL2 (hit / corrupt / miss), writeBehind (NX, pending set), set (plain SET + publish), delete (tombstone + publish), onMessage (apna id ignore, l1.delete), onResubscribed (l1.clear), withTimeout (l2TimeoutMs, timer unref'd), call() jo kabhi throw nahi karta, redisTtl (whole ms rounded up, Infinity = no expiry). src/cached.ts: @Cached legacy method decorator -- key.apply(this, args) (key function ko instance this ke roop mein milta hai; pehli version mein nahi milta tha, D5), undefined key = uncached, cache.getOrLoad ke through, pehle caller ka this, hamesha promise (sync throw = rejection, D6). src/adapters/http.ts: Loadable interface (LruCache aur TwoLevelCache dono fit), CacheKeyFn, requestSignal (response close aur not writableFinished), loadForRequest (ran flag + refresh flag -> hit / stale / miss / bypass), isNotFound, NOT_FOUND_BODY. src/adapters/express.ts: cachedJson -- destroyed / ended response par kuch nahi likhta, aborted signal par next(err) nahi. src/adapters/nestjs.ts: CachedRouteInterceptor (next.handle() sirf miss par, X-Cache header, NotFoundException) aur @CachedRoute = applyDecorators(UseInterceptors(new instance)), @Cached re-export. src/index.ts: core exports; express aur nestjs alag entry points (package.json exports), @nestjs/common aur rxjs optional peer dependencies. test/: support.ts (manual clock, deferred, event recorder), fake-redis.ts (test clock par TTLs, down / hang modes, held pub/sub messages), aur 14 test files, 178 tests: lru 16, ttl 15, load 21, stats-events 6, model 9, swr 25, negative 11, two-level 35, adapters 5, redis-l2 8, express-helper 10, nestjs-helper 5, cached 8, adapters-unit 4. vitest.config.ts: 20 s test aur hook timeouts, sirf busy machine ke liye. bench/overhead.mjs: dist build ke against per-operation cost, results bench/reference-results/ mein (run1, run2, aur before-iterator-fix).
difficult_decisions: LRU ek JavaScript Map par, hand-written doubly linked list + hash map nahi. Map insertion order mein iterate karta hai, toh pehli key least recently used hai aur hit = delete + set. Node objects nahi, code bahut kam, galti ki jagah kam. Catch benchmark ne dikhaya: victim har baar naye iterator se nahi, ek long-lived keys() iterator se lena padta hai -- spec ke hisaab se woh deleted entries skip karta hai aur baad mein append hui entries visit karta hai, aur har live key uski position ke baad hi hoti hai.

Abort ka rule: caller abort kare toh sirf USKA wait rukta hai; load ka signal tab abort hota hai jab har waiter chala jaaye, aur tab flight detach hoti hai taaki agla caller fresh load kare, cancelled load join na kare. Pehle caller par cancel karna ek impatient client se sabko fail karwata; kabhi cancel na karna aisa DB kaam jo koi nahi chahta. Signal ke bina caller kabhi nahi jaata, toh load zinda rakhta hai; aur background refresh mein cache khud ek permanent waiter hai, taaki join karke abort karne wala caller refresh cancel na kare.

Load versions: flight object hi key ka version hai. delete, set aur clear running load ko detach karte hain, aur load sirf tab likhta hai jab woh abhi bhi attached ho. Isse 'row update ki, delete(key) kiya, aur update se pehle shuru hua slow load purani row wapas likh gaya' wala bug band hota hai. Jo callers already wait kar rahe the unhe wahi result milta hai -- unhone wahi maanga tha. Yahi idea stage 2 mein LoadContext.isCurrent() bana, jisse TwoLevelCache Redis write rokta hai.

Stale-while-revalidate sirf getOrLoad mein: get / peek / has stale entry ko absent maante hain, kyunki get ke paas loader nahi, refresh shuru nahi kar sakta, aur stale lautane se har non-loading caller ke liye ttlMs bemaani ho jaata. Failed refresh stale value rakhta hai (grace ka matlab hi slow ya failing backend jhelna hai), backoff nahi (zyada state; not implemented). Errors kabhi cache nahi -- ek 50 ms blip poore error TTL ka outage ban jaata; negative caching sirf LOADED 'not found' values par, min(TTL, negativeTtlMs) aur bina grace ke.

Cross-replica writes: load ke baad Redis write SET NX, aur delete DEL ki jagah tombstone (default 10 s). Alternatives the: Lua compare-and-set with per-key version keys (zyada moving parts) aur 'delayed double delete' (sleep, phir bhi window). Saath mein Redis kabhi read fail nahi karta: har call l2TimeoutMs (250 ms) se bounded, failure = miss + l2-error event, set / delete boolean dete hain throw nahi -- DB write ho chuka hai, cache problem ke liye 500 galat hota.

Framework helpers HTTP bytes nahi, handler ka DATA cache karte hain: res.write intercept karke replay karna streaming, headers aur status codes par toot-ta hai. Key function required hai, koi default nahi: coalescing mein sirf PEHLE request ka producer chalta hai, toh URL-only default ek user ka data doosre ko de deta. Request ka disconnect signal getOrLoad mein jaata hai -- stage 1 ka 'sab jaayein tab abort' rule reuse, nayi cancellation logic nahi. Nest helper ek interceptor INSTANCE hai (DI nahi), jaise ratelimit-kit ka guard.
biggest_challenges: Eviction O(1) nahi thi -- benchmark ne pakda, tests ne nahi. Pehli version victim ko this.map.entries().next() se dhundhti thi: 10401.9 ns per evicting set, Map.get se lagbhag 150x. Likely reason (V8 source maine nahi padha, sirf fix ka effect measure kiya): V8 har deleted entry ke liye table mein hole chhodta hai rehash tak, aur naya iterator slot 0 se shuru hota hai, toh har eviction pichhli evictions ke saare holes par chalti thi. Fix: ek long-lived keys() iterator -- ab 548.8 / 664.6 ns. Purana code wapas daalne wala mutation L8 pehle KOI test fail nahi karta tha (pure performance change); timing assertions is machine par flaky the, toh ab ek test 1000 evictions mein Map.prototype.keys calls ginta hai (at most 1).

Cross-replica race jo sirf real Redis test ne pakdi. Replica B miss karta hai aur DB se PURANI row padhta hai; replica A row update karke set() karta hai; B ka background write apne connection par A ke write ke BAAD Redis pahunchta hai -- aur Redis poore TTL ke liye purani value har replica ko deta raha (pehli version ka 'set on A: B reads the new value' test bilkul aise hi fail hua). Fix SET NX + tombstone; ab real-Redis race test 20 rounds chalata hai, aur chaar recorded runs mein NX refusal 6, 14, 17 aur 11 rounds mein hit hua (baaki mein message pehle pahuncha), Redis mein har baar A ki value. Dono orders fake Redis par held messages se deterministic tests bhi hain.

Mutation W5 ne test run HANG kar diya. 'remove par weight subtract nahi' wala break weight-eviction loop ko hamesha ke liye ghuma deta tha: map khaali, total phir bhi limit ke upar. Runner ka 300 s timeout sirf shell ko maarta tha, 12 orphaned node processes ghoomte rahe aur baad ke checks slow karte rahe jab tak haath se nahi maare. Do changes: loop ab tab bhi rukta hai jab sirf nayi entry bachi ho (size > 1 -- sahi bookkeeping mein no-op, isliye W8 equivalent survivor hai), taaki bookkeeping bug hang nahi, dikhne wali galat evictions de; aur weights integer only, kyunki 0.1 + 0.2 - 0.1 - 0.2 = 2.8e-17, 0 nahi (naya break W7). Runner ab poora process tree maarta hai.

ioredis ka 'ready' event jhooth bolta hai -- matlab 'listening again' nahi. Reconnect ke baad L1 clear karna zaroori hai kyunki disconnect ke dauraan publish hue messages kho jaate hain. Lekin ioredis 5.4.1 ke event_handler.js mein padha ki ready apna re-SUBSCRIBE bhejne se PEHLE emit hota hai; ready par clear karte toh ek gap rehta jismein message miss ho ke L1 mein purani value phir aa sakti. Adapter ab ready par khud SUBSCRIBE bhejta hai aur onResubscribed sirf Redis ke confirm karne par chalata hai; mutation X17 (ready par hi call) aur X18 (pehla ready reconnect maana) dono tests pakadte hain.

Stage 3 ke 'client already gone' survivors: pehli mutation run mein C4 (finished response ke baad bhi abort), E1 (gone client ko send) aur E2 (gone client ke liye next(err)) survive kar gaye. Reason: real socket par closed connection mein likhna chupchaap drop ho jaata hai, toh real-app test kuch dekh hi nahi sakta. test/adapters-unit.test.ts ek fake response object se yeh paths observable banata hai; ab 20 mein se 20 caught (C7, D5, D6 interview-bank review ke teen fixes guard karte hain). Stage 2 mein bhi yahi lesson tha: 4 first-run survivors (X15, X16, X24, X25) equivalent nahi, test gaps the -- jaise X15 wala test hung Redis read ke timeout se pehle hi check kar leta tha.
failure_scenarios: Redis down ya hang: har Redis call l2TimeoutMs (default 250 ms) par give up. Failed ya timed-out read = miss, loader chalta hai, L1 cache karta hai; writes chupchaap fail (l2-error events, l2Errors); set / delete false resolve karte hain, throw nahi. Tested: fake Redis down / never answering, ioredis aise port par jahan kuch nahi sun raha, aur connection mid-run kill. ioredis ka enableOfflineQueue: false rakho, warna disconnected hone par har command timeout tak wait karegi.

Subscriber disconnect: pub/sub fire-and-forget hai, disconnect ke dauraan publish hua message kho jaata hai aur us replica ka L1 purani value deta hai. Mitigation: har re-subscribe par poora L1 clear (Redis se refill, DB se nahi), sirf confirmed SUBSCRIBE ke baad. Jo connection half-open hai aur abhi dead detect nahi hua, woh sirf L1 TTL se bounded hai -- isliye shared data ke liye L1 TTL chhota (seconds) rakho. Real Redis par CLIENT KILL se tested: reconnect, L1 clear, invalidations phir aati hain.

Database outage stale-while-revalidate ke saath: stale value grace khatam hone tak serve hoti rehti hai, refresh-error events. Lekin backoff nahi: hot stale key outage mein ek-ek karke back to back refresh bhejti hai. Grace ke baad key plain miss hai, caller loader ka wait karta hai aur error paata hai; errors cache nahi hote, toh har miss loader tak jaata hai (concurrent callers ke liye single flight phir bhi, per key ek load at a time).

Loader jo kabhi settle nahi hota aur signal ignore karta hai: bina signal wale callers ke liye key ki flight hamesha ke liye atak jaati hai; background refresh ho toh us key ka koi naya refresh nahi, aur grace ke baad har caller atke refresh ko join karta hai. Fix library mein nahi: loader ke andar timeout lagao (jaise projects/18-resilience ka TimeoutPolicy) aur load signal DB driver ko pass karo.

Remaining consistency windows of TwoLevelCache: (a) delete ke tombstoneMs se zyada baad pahunchne wala load write purani value wapas likh deta hai -- tombstoneMs loader timeout se upar rakho; (b) silently cut-off subscriber L1 TTL tak purani copy deta hai; (c) A ke set aur message ke B tak pahunchne ke beech B purani L1 copy deta hai (healthy network par milliseconds); (d) set / delete false lautaayein toh baaki replicas aur Redis TTL tak purani value rakh sakte hain; (e) Redis ki corrupt (decode na hone wali) value plain SET se overwrite hoti hai, NX nahi -- us gap mein doosre replica ka set overwrite ho sakta hai; (f) tombstone ek normal Redis key hai -- memory pressure mein evict ho ya Redis bina persistence restart ho toh late NX write phir accept; (g) ioredis subscriber adapter failed re-SUBSCRIBE ignore karta hai -- ioredis ka apna resubscribe chal jaaye toh messages aate hain par L1 clear nahi hua (L1 TTL se bounded). Saath mein TwoLevelCache.set Redis likhta hai chahe L1 value ko too heavy maan ke refuse kare. Yeh cache hai, consistency protocol nahi.

Galat cache key: helpers mein key required hai aur coalescing mein sirf pehle request ka producer chalta hai, toh per-user data ki key mein user na ho toh ek user ka data doosre ko jaata hai (test: alice, bob, alice -> miss, miss, hit, sabko apna data). @Cached pehle caller ka this aur arguments use karta hai, isliye key function ko instance this ke roop mein milta hai (key: function (this: Tenant) { ... }; arrow function this nahi dekh sakta) -- ek test jaan-boojh ke galat key (arrow) dikhata hai jismein tenant b ko tenant a ka config milta hai, aur ek test sahi per-tenant key. Pehli version key ko this deti hi nahi thi (bank review mein pakda, fix, mutation D5).
improvements: Refresh backoff aur refresh-ahead: abhi failed refresh agle stale read par turant retry hota hai, toh DB outage mein hot key back-to-back refresh bhejti hai. Per-key backoff (exponential, jitter ke saath) aur ek refresh-ahead jo hot key ko stale hone se PEHLE refresh kare -- dono not implemented.

Invalidation transport: pub/sub fire-and-forget hai aur half-open connection L1 TTL tak stale rakhta hai. RESP3 client-side caching (CLIENT TRACKING) server-pushed invalidations deta, ya Redis Streams ek durable log jise reconnect karne wala replica replay kar sake. Dono not implemented; abhi ka safety net chhota L1 TTL aur re-subscribe par L1 clear hai.

Redis Cluster / Sentinel: adapters sirf ek Redis 7.4.12 server ke against tested hain; failover, MOVED redirects aur cluster mein pub/sub ka behaviour test nahi hua. Saath mein replicas ke beech clear() (Redis prefix saaf karne ke liye SCAN chahiye) aur non-string keys ke liye L2 -- abhi nahi bane.

HTTP caching semantics: helpers sirf handler data cache karte hain; Cache-Control, ETag, Vary aur conditional requests nahi, non-JSON ya streamed responses nahi. PLAN ke hisaab se yeh reverse proxy ya CDN better karta hai, lekin ETag / 304 helper useful hota. NestJS on Fastify aur Express 5 ka test bhi pending.

Performance measurement: stage 2 ka overhead measure hi nahi hua (hit path par fresh/stale comparison aur negative check jude), Redis round trips bhi nahi, concurrency, memory per entry aur Linux bhi nahi. Stage 1 numbers bhi busy machine par the (Map floor 36.9 se 78.9 ns tak hila), aur yeh investigate nahi kiya ki hit lagbhag 400 ns kyun leta hai -- delete + set ya performance.now(). Idle machine par dobara chalana chahiye.

Admission aur sizing: abhi pure LRU hai; LFU / W-TinyLFU admission (jo Caffeine karta hai) scan-type traffic se hot keys bachata. weigh har set par chalta hai, toh JSON.stringify jaisa mehnga weigh write path par lagta hai; object walk karke size estimate nahi hai. Aur package private hai -- npm publish ke liye versioning, changelog aur CI (Redis service ke saath) chahiye.

learning_path.concept: LRU on a JavaScript Map, bounded by entries and weight
steps: 1. Concept: LRU cache full hone par least recently used entry nikaalta hai. Map insertion order yaad rakhta hai, toh pehli key = LRU, aur hit par delete + set = key end par.
2. Project need: cache bina bound ke ek slow memory leak hai; aur values ke size bahut alag hon (chhota user, bada catalog) toh sirf entry count kaafi nahi -- bytes ka bound bhi chahiye.
3. Code/API: cache.ts new LruCache({ maxEntries, maxWeight, weigh }); get / peek / has / set / delete / clear, size, totalWeight, keys().

4. Detail: exactly limit par kuch evict nahi; set pehle size loop phir weight loop chalata hai; maxWeight se bhaari single value store nahi hoti (set false, reject event) aur key ki purani value hat jaati hai; weigh integer >= 0 warna RangeError aur cache unchanged; weight loop mein size > 1 guard (W5 hang ke baad); victim ek long-lived keys() iterator se, kyunki naya iterator har baar V8 ke holes par chalta tha (10401.9 -> 548.8 / 664.6 ns).

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/lru.test.ts -- 'exactly at maxEntries nothing is evicted', 'a single value heavier than maxWeight is not stored', aur 'evictions reuse one Map iterator' (1000 evictions, at most 1 Map.prototype.keys call).
6. Interviewer next: linked list + hash map se kya fark hai, aur ek scan (ek baar padhi jaane wali bahut saari keys) LRU ko kaise kharab karta hai?

learning_path.concept: TTL: lazy expiry, a monotonic clock and an unref'd sweep
steps: 1. Concept: TTL = entry kitni der valid hai. Lazy expiry har read par check karti hai (timer ke bina); sweep sirf un expired entries ki memory chhudata hai jinhe koi padhta nahi.
2. Project need: expired value kabhi return nahi honi chahiye, aur cache kabhi process ko exit hone se nahi rokna chahiye.
3. Code/API: LruCache({ ttlMs, sweepIntervalMs, now }), set(key, value, { ttlMs }), purgeExpired(), close().

4. Detail: set time t par ttlMs 100 -> t + 99 tak live, t + 100 PAR expired; TTL set se ginti hai, read se nahi (sliding expiry nahi); per-entry ttlMs default override karta hai, Infinity kabhi expire nahi; expired eviction victim 'expired' reason se report; default clock performance.now (monotonic -- NTP ya VM resume sab kuch ek saath expire na kare); sweep setInterval unref'd, close() do baar bhi theek.
5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/ttl.test.ts -- 'boundary: live 1 ms before ttlMs, expired AT ttlMs', 'is unref'd: it never keeps the process alive' (hasRef() false).
6. Interviewer next: size() mein expired entries kyun gini jaati hain, aur TTL ko read par refresh karna (sliding) kab galat hai?
1. Concept: cache stampede = cold key par bahut saare concurrent misses, sab DB ko same query bhejte hain. Single flight: per key ek load, baaki usse join karte hain.
2. Project need: ek popular key expire hote hi 100 requests 100 queries na banein; aur jo client chala gaya uske liye DB kaam na chalta rahe -- lekin ek client ke jaane se baaki fail na hon.
3. Code/API: getOrLoad(key, (loadSignal, context) => ..., { signal, ttlMs }); stats().coalesced; events load / load-error / load-abort.

4. Detail: flights map mein Flight { controller, promise, waiters }; error sab waiters ko, cache nahi, agla call phir load; sync throw bhi rejection; abort par caller signal.reason se reject, waiters-- ; aakhri waiter gaya toh controller.abort aur flight detach (agla caller fresh load, abandoned load kuch nahi likhta); signal ke bina caller kabhi nahi jaata; settle par listener remove; already-aborted caller na start na join.

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/load.test.ts -- '100 concurrent getOrLoad for one key -> the loader runs ONCE' (99 coalesced), 'ALL waiters abort: the load's signal is aborted, nothing is written'.
6. Interviewer next: errors ko thodi der cache kyun nahi kiya, aur ek loader jo kabhi settle nahi hota uska kya hota hai?
1. Concept: ek async load jo invalidation se pehle shuru hua, invalidation ke baad khatam hokar purani value likh sakta hai. Har load ko ek version do aur sirf current version ko likhne do.
2. Project need: updateUser() row update karke delete(id) karta hai; agar update se pehle shuru hua slow load baad mein likh de toh cache purani row TTL bhar serve karega.
3. Code/API: cache.ts mein Flight object hi version hai; delete / set / clear flights.delete(key) karte hain; LoadContext.isCurrent() = flights.get(key) === flight.

4. Detail: startLoad ke async block mein loader ke baad check -- abhi bhi attached ho tabhi store; waiting callers ko wahi result milta hai; purana load fail ho toh naye flight ko detach nahi karta (sirf apna hi hataata hai); projects/18-resilience ke breaker generations wala hi idea; stage 2 mein TwoLevelCache isCurrent() se Redis write bhi rokta hai.

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/load.test.ts -t 'stale writes' -- delete / clear / set during a load, aur 'an old load failing after delete() does not remove the new load in flight'. Mutation F3 (version check hataya) stage-2 run mein 151 mein se 9 tests fail karta hai.
6. Interviewer next: distributed setup mein yahi problem kaise dikhti hai (iska jawab NX + tombstone hai), aur version ke liye counter vs object identity?
1. Concept: SWR -- TTL ke baad ek grace jismein purani value turant milti hai aur background mein ek refresh chalta hai. Negative caching -- 'not found' ko bhi cache karna, lekin chhote TTL ke liye.
2. Project need: hot key expire hone par users ko DB latency na dikhe, slow ya failing DB jhela ja sake; aur missing id ke flood (bots, typos) har baar DB tak na jaaye.
3. Code/API: LruCache({ staleMs, negativeTtlMs, isNegative }); stats staleHits, refreshes, refreshErrors, negativeHits; events refresh / refresh-error.

4. Detail: fresh [t, t+ttl), stale [t+ttl, t+ttl+staleMs), gone uske baad; refresh ek normal flight (set / delete / clear jeet-te hain) jismein cache ek permanent waiter hai; failed refresh stale value rakhta hai, agla stale read retry (backoff nahi); get / peek / has stale nahi lautaate; negative value min(TTL, negativeTtlMs), koi grace nahi; set(key, null) negative nahi; errors phir bhi cache nahi.

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/swr.test.ts test/negative.test.ts -- '50 concurrent stale reads start ONE refresh', 'keeps serving the stale value until the grace ends', '1000 sequential + 100 concurrent -> ONE loader call'.
6. Interviewer next: staleMs kitna rakhoge aur kaunsa data stale serve nahi hona chahiye (jaise balance)? Errors ko negative cache kyun nahi kiya?

learning_path.concept: Two-level cache: Redis L2, SET NX and tombstones
steps: 1. Concept: L1 har process ke andar (fast, per replica), L2 Redis mein (sab replicas share karte hain). Read: L1 -> L2 -> loader; write dono mein.
2. Project need: N replicas har ek miss par apna DB load na karein; ek replica ka load baaki ko Redis se mil jaaye -- lekin purani value kabhi Redis mein 'jeet' na jaaye.
3. Code/API: two-level.ts new TwoLevelCache({ l1, redis: ioredisL2Client(redis), subscriber, prefix, codec, l2TimeoutMs, tombstoneMs }); getOrLoad, set, delete, flush, close, stats().

4. Detail: Redis read L1 load ke andar (50 misses -> 1 read + 1 load); MULTI GET + PTTL; L1 copy ko min(PTTL, call TTL); load ke baad write-behind SET PX NX (await nahi), corrupt value ho toh bina NX overwrite; set plain SET; delete tombstone tombstoneMs ke liye; NX refusal = l2WritesSkipped; TTL whole ms rounded up; jsonCodec {v: ...} envelope aur uski losses (Date string ban jaata hai, Map {} ); har call l2TimeoutMs bounded, failure = miss.

5. Demo: docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml up -d redis, phir cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/two-level.test.ts test/redis-l2.test.ts -- dono 'RACE' tests (held messages ke saath fake Redis, aur real Redis par 20 rounds jo console mein NX refusal count print karta hai).
6. Interviewer next: tombstoneMs loader timeout se kam ho toh kya hoga, aur Lua compare-and-set kab better hai?
1. Concept: Redis pub/sub -- PUBLISH channel par, saare SUBSCRIBE-d connections ko message. Fire-and-forget: jo us waqt connected nahi, usse message nahi milta.
2. Project need: replica A par update hua toh B, C ke L1 se purani copy turant hatni chahiye, TTL ka wait nahi.
3. Code/API: L2Subscriber.subscribe(channel, onMessage, onResubscribed); ioredisSubscriber(redis.duplicate()); events invalidated / resubscribed; channel default prefix + 'invalidate'.

4. Detail: message [instanceId, key] JSON; apna id ignore (sender ka naya value bach jaaye); onMessage -> l1.delete jo running load bhi detach karta hai; malformed message l2-error; doosra connection kyunki subscriber mode mein GET / SET nahi; reconnect par poora L1 clear, lekin ioredis ready re-SUBSCRIBE se pehle aata hai, isliye adapter khud SUBSCRIBE bhej ke confirm par clear karta hai; half-open connection sirf L1 TTL se bounded.

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/adapters.test.ts -t 'CONFIRMED', aur test/two-level.test.ts -t 'MISSES messages' -- disconnected subscriber purani value deta hai jab tak reconnect L1 clear na kare; redis-l2.test.ts mein CLIENT KILL wala test real Redis par.
6. Interviewer next: CLIENT TRACKING ya Redis Streams pub/sub ki jagah kya dete (yahan not implemented), aur L1 TTL kitna rakhoge?

learning_path.concept: Framework helpers: cache data, a required key, X-Cache and the disconnect signal
steps: 1. Concept: route ya service method ke result ko cache karna, request se key nikal ke; response bytes nahi, handler ka data.
2. Project need: owner ke Express aur NestJS services mein har route par getOrLoad haath se likhna repeat aur error-prone hai -- aur galat key data leak hai.

3. Code/API: adapters/express.ts cachedJson(cache, { key, ttlMs, staleMs, notFound }, (req, signal) => ...); adapters/nestjs.ts @CachedRoute(cache, options) aur CachedRouteInterceptor; cached.ts @Cached(cache, { key, ttlMs }); adapters/http.ts requestSignal, loadForRequest.

4. Detail: key undefined -> bypass; ran flag -> hit / miss, aur is request ke background refresh ne producer chalaya toh stale (pehle yeh 'miss' dikhta tha, C7); null / undefined -> 404 aur cached; error next(err) / Nest exception layer, cached nahi; requestSignal response close par abort jab tak finish na hua ho; Express mein gone client ko na write na next(err) (Nest mein special case nahi: aborted wait exception layer mein, no-op write; Nest handler ko abort signal nahi); @Cached pehle caller ka this aur args use karta hai, key function ko this milta hai (D5), sync throw rejection (D6), AbortSignal nahi; Nest interceptor ek instance (DI nahi), hit par handler chalta hi nahi.

5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/express-helper.test.ts test/nestjs-helper.test.ts test/cached.test.ts test/adapters-unit.test.ts -- 'per-user data', '20 concurrent requests for one key: ONE producer call', 'every waiting client disconnects', 'two Express instances' (Redis chahiye).
6. Interviewer next: HTTP caching (Cache-Control, ETag) se yeh kaise alag hai aur kab CDN better hai? Per-user key mein tenant ya locale bhool gaye toh kya?

learning_path.concept: Testing honestly: a model test, mutation checks and the benchmark
steps: 1. Concept: model-based testing = implementation ko ek simple, obviously-correct model ke against random steps par compare karna. Mutation check = jaan-boojh ke bug daalo, suite chalao, dekho koi test fail hota hai ya nahi.
2. Project need: LRU + TTL + weight + stale + negative ke combinations haath se likhe tests cover nahi kar sakte; aur '178 tests pass' yeh nahi batata ki tests kuch pakadte hain.
3. Code/API: test/model.test.ts (mulberry32 seeded PRNG, naive array Model); README ke 'Mutation checks' tables; bench/overhead.mjs aur bench/reference-results/.

4. Detail: 8 seeds x 3000 steps, har step ke baad return value, key order, total weight aur poore stats identical; aakhri test check karta hai ki har rule (hits, misses, rejects, teeno eviction reasons, stale aur negative hits) 50 se zyada baar hit hua. Mutations: stage 1 42 breaks (39 caught, 3 equivalent), stage 2 99 (96 caught, same 3 equivalent, 4 first-run gaps closed), stage 3 20 (sab caught; kul 119 distinct breaks). Benchmark: busy machine, isliye orders of magnitude -- lekin isne 10401.9 ns eviction pakdi.
5. Demo: cd projects/20-cache && npx vitest run test/model.test.ts (coverage line print hoti hai), npm test (178 tests), aur npm run bench (build + bench/reference-results/<date>-<platform>.json).
6. Interviewer next: equivalent mutant kaise pehchanoge (L6, L7, W8), aur benchmark ka number machine ki wajah se galat hai yeh kaise pata chalega?
